chapter_title_en: The Attrition of a Fiendgod Clone
chapter_seo_title: Desolate Era Ch. 231 – Ji Ning Defeats a Fiendgod Clone Through Pure Attrition
chapter_meta_description: Ji Ning faces a golden-armored Fiendgod clone in the War God Hall. Instead of close combat, he uses Starseizing Hand archery and formation tactics to drain the clone’s divine power and secure a stunning ranged victory.
og_title: Ji Ning Outsmarts a Fiendgod Clone from a Hundred Yards
og_description: The third level of the War God Hall throws a devastating Fiendgod clone at Ji Ning. He doesn’t rush in—he pulls back, draws his bow, and shoots until the ancient general crumbles.
twitter_title: When a Fiendgod clone demands close combat, Ji Ning says: “No thanks.” 🏹
twitter_description: Ji Ning uses Starseizing Hand archery and formation sword-light to wear down a Fiendgod clone from a distance. The estate spirit is stunned.

lore_anchors.definition: A doppelganger formed from a sliver of a powerful Fiendgod's divine power. Cut off from the main body, its energy is non-renewable, making it vulnerable to attrition tactics.
A top-ten divine ability since Pangu's era; allows a cultivator to use their hands as ultimate weapons for close combat or archery.
A mid-range sword formation that links multiple flying swords into a coordinated attack. At the ninth level, it rivals close-combat power for a late-Wanxiang cultivator.
A unique Dao technique created by Ji Ning, manifesting as counter-rotating lotus petals of water and fire that bind and crush enemies.
A movement-type divine ability of the Yuchi clan that condenses wings of divine power for rapid travel.
The second tier of graded magic treasures (Mortal, Earth, Heaven, Immortal); suitable for mid-to-high level cultivators.
A soul-based perceptual and telekinetic power, normally unlocked at the Primal Daoist stage; Ji Ning wields it anomalously at Wanxiang.
The fourth and highest substage of the Wanxiang Adept realm, where the cultivator's Violet Palace develops a perfect star, moon, and sun for peak Ki circulation.
